Ahura Mazda identifies this primordial word as the Ahuna-vairya, assigns high ritual value to its correct recitation, promises to bring the reciter's soul over the Bridge of Alnvat to Heaven, and warns that removing portions from it causes the soul to be drawn away from the better world. The passage also says the saying contains Ahu and Ratu, was pronounced before creation, and that the more bountiful of the two Spirits declared the whole creation across present, emerging, and future man, Daevas, Khrafstra-men, the incarnate world, and Mazda-made good creatures.","category":"speech","evidence_refs":["ev:2"]},{"id":"obs:3","text":"Ahura Mazda identifies the word as the Ahuna-vairya stanzas.","category":"attribute","evidence_refs":["ev:4"]},{"id":"obs:5","text":"A person in the corporeal world who mentally recalls, undertones, utters aloud, or chants the Ahuna-vairya in worship heaven.","category":"action","evidence_refs":["ev:5"]},{"id":"obs:6","text":"A person who takes away a portion of the Ahuna-vairya, whether half, third, fourth, or fifth, is warned that Ahura Mazda
